name: Patchwork Thermal Legging
description: A pair of thermal leggings assembled from at least three different source garments — you can see where the textures change at mid-thigh and again below the knee, stitched together with a running seam in black thread. Colors are a mismatched gradient of dark grey, faded olive, and near-black. Warm, ugly, and entirely practical for a Shelf winter.
functionality: Multi-layer thermal construction traps heat effectively; worn under trousers or alone in warmer months.
what_it_says: Function over form, assembled from what was available — this person wastes nothing.
worn_by: elderly shelf residents who feel the cold
manufacturer: Handmade — no brand, market stall or self-made
story_hooks: One panel is cut from a child's garment — the scale of the print gives it away, small cartoon shapes barely visible under the grey dye.
A Shelf seamstress sells these at the Ruck Market and can identify her own stitching — useful if you need to prove where something came from.
related_entities: Helix Biosystems NeuroSalve Cortical Repair Gel NR-2200

physical_description.visual_profile: Visibly patched thermal leggings showing clear seam lines where three separate garments were stitched together. The mismatched color blocks create an unintentional gradient effect running vertically down the legs, reading as industrial salvage rather than intentional design. Silhouette is functional and form-fitting without being sleek—honest wear-and-repair aesthetic.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight through the calves and thighs, following the body without restriction. The fit varies slightly where patches meet due to differing source garment stretch. No excess fabric at ankles or waist—designed for layering under heavier outer wear.
physical_description.primary_material: Mixed thermal synthetics—likely recycled performance fabric from athletic or work garments, each panel retaining its original weave characteristics. Non-uniform thickness indicates multiple manufacturing origins.
physical_description.texture: Varied surface—some panels show tight ribbed thermal knit, others a smoother stretched fleece-backed synthetic. Black running seams are visible and slightly raised where panels overlap. Overall tactile impression is rough-functional, not refined.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dark grey, faded olive-green, and near-black in large irregular blocks. No pattern intentionality—colors vary due to fading and source material age. Creates an unplanned three-tone striped effect.
physical_description.closures: None visible—pull-on high-waist design, likely with a simple elastic or drawstring waistband (obscured).
distinctive_features: Visible black running stitch seams joining three distinct fabric panels
Clear texture shifts at mid-thigh and below-knee junctures
Uneven color grading suggesting different garment ages and wear histories
Slightly puckered seams where different fabric densities meet
Signs of hand-stitching irregularity—human-made repair work
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 sub-grade / Tier 4 working class boundary—handmade salvage wear that prioritizes function over appearance.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street-tier, shelf-dweller, industrial worker, or climate refugee. Signals resourcefulness, poverty, and survival pragmatism rather than aesthetic choice. Worn by people who cannot afford new thermal base layers and adapt what they find.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn-in and patched, showing age without active distressing. The garment is already broken-in from its previous lives. Some faint pilling on lower panels, seams holding firm but not pristine.
